The gradient vector \nabla f(a,b) at a point P = (a,b) and several unit vectors \vec{r}, \vec{s}, \vec{t}, \vec{u}, \vec{n}, and \vec{e} in the xy-plane are shown in the figure. You may assume that angles that look the same are the same. Here, f_{\vec{v}} \, (a,b) denotes the directional derivative, which is often written as D_{\vec{v}} \, f(a,b). Are the following statements true or false?
f_{\vec{e}} \, (a,b) = \langle 0, 0 \rangle.
f_{\vec{r}} \, (a,b) \lt f_{\vec{s}} \, (a,b).
f_{\vec{u}} \, (a,b) = f_{\vec{t}} \, (a,b).
f_{\vec{n}} \, (a,b) = || \nabla f(a,b) ||.
f_{\vec{r}} \, (a,b) = f_{\vec{t}} \, (a,b).
f_{\vec{r}} \, (a,b) \lt f_{\vec{u}} \, (a,b).
f_{\vec{s}} \, (a,b) points in the direction of minimum rate of change of f.
f_{\vec{r}} \, (a,b) \lt 0.
